before:
Tidal Mill Trust — Sluice Attendance Manual

Attendants on the night watch hold three standing tasks: keeping the head pond within its marked band, keeping the fish pass wetted, and keeping the visitor channel clear for the morning demonstration. Where the inflow will not serve all three at once, the head pond is served before the fish pass, and the fish pass before the visitor channel. No task is ever abandoned; the attendant simply works down the list until the water runs out, then resumes at the top when the flood returns. Any night on which the visitor channel goes dry for more than two hours is written up in the watch book and passed to the Wednesday meeting for comment.

Moorland Bothy Association — Autumn Fuel Bulletin

Wardens report that the two upper bothies are again receiving driftwood and pallet timber carried up from the valley car park. The Association reminds members that visitors may bring in seasoned hardwood for the stove, provided it is stored on the raised slats and not on the earth floor. Painted or treated timber is not to be burned in any hut under Association care, on account of the flue linings replaced last spring. Members finding treated timber in a fuel store should set it aside by the door and note the hut in the visitors' book, so the next warden round can carry it down.

Coastal Path Volunteers — Boardwalk Handbook, Section 5

Section 5 covers the reed-bed crossing between the sluice and the hide. The timber deck there rests on driven piles which, on the evidence of the two pits opened in 2019, are thought to reach roughly 1.8 metres into the peat. Volunteers should not drive fixings deeper than the deck bearers without asking the works officer, since the pile heads sit close beneath. Loose boards are lifted, the bearer inspected, and the board refixed with the longer screws kept in the green tin. Any board showing rot along more than half its bearing is taken out of the walk entirely and marked for the winter replacement run.

before:
Seed Bank — Annual Accession Report, Working Method

This year the accession bench was rearranged to shorten handling time. Incoming packets are now weighed, then dried in the cabinet, then counted onto the tally sheet, then sealed into foil. The germination sample is drawn as before, at whatever point the operator finds convenient, and the moisture reading is taken once at the end. Nothing in the acceptance standard has moved: packets below the stated germination figure are still refused, and every accession still carries the collector's slip into the cold store. Staff report that the bench arrangement suits the smaller autumn intake better than the summer one, and the point will be looked at again in spring.

before:
Depot Stores — Reorder Settings Sheet

These settings drive the nightly reorder run for consumable stock at the northern depot. Reorder points for each line are calculated using the twelve-week moving average of issues, with the supplier lead time taken from the vendor table. Lines flagged as seasonal are excluded from the run and ordered by hand. The stores clerk reviews the proposed order each morning and may strike any line before release. Emergency orders raised outside the run are entered against the same cost codes and appear on the weekly print. Nothing here changes what the depot is obliged to hold under the maintenance agreement; that list is kept separately and is not touched by the nightly job.

before:
Allotment Society — Waiting List Transfer Process

Each quarter the site secretary sends the waiting list to the parish clerk for the public notice board. The list is exported from the office spreadsheet as one line per applicant, with surname, initial, date of application and preferred plot size separated by semicolons. The clerk pastes the file into the notice template without editing. Applicants are never reordered on transfer; the sequence in the file is the sequence on the board. Where an applicant has asked for their name to be withheld, the line carries the application date alone. Errors spotted on the board are corrected at the office end and the file resent, never amended on the printed sheet.

before:
Common Grazing Registry — Notes on Entries

For the purposes of this registry, a working share means a share on which stock has been put out in at least one of the previous three years. Working shares carry a vote at the graziers' meeting, are counted in the stint calculation, and are the shares against which the summer dues are raised. Shares outside that description remain on the register but are shown in the second column and carry none of the above. The clerk reviews the columns each May against the marking returns. Transfers between holdings are entered on the date of the deed, whatever the state of the share at the time of transfer.
